A `<Transition>` around the backdrop animates it, in place of `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style` and the `transitionStatus` of the state. A closed backdrop leaves the DOM, or has `[hidden]` with `keepMounted`, so it needs no `data-open` and `data-closed`.

A `<Transition>` around the popup animates it, in place of `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style` and the `transitionStatus` of the state. A closed popup leaves the DOM, or has `[hidden]` with `keepMounted`, so it needs no `data-open` and `data-closed`.

The viewport is new in the DOM at each open, so a CSS animation on it runs at the open. `:has(> .v-leave-active)` selects it while its popup leaves, and `[hidden]` while `keepMounted` keeps it closed. These take the place of `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style`, `data-open`, `data-closed` and the `transitionStatus` of the state.
